Position Title: Data Scientist III
Location: Arlington, VA – Hybrid (Candidates must reside in the DC Metro area and report to the Arlington, VA office twice per pay period.)
Clearance Requirements: Public Trust Clearance (Candidates must be eligible to obtain a Position of Public Trust clearance.)
Position Status: Contract

Position Description:
Seneca Resources is seeking an experienced Data Scientist III to support advanced data analytics, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and business intelligence initiatives in a complex enterprise environment. This role is ideal for a data science professional who enjoys transforming structured and unstructured data into actionable insights, developing scalable analytical solutions, and communicating complex findings to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
The Data Scientist will work across data engineering, analytics, visualization, AI/ML, and cloud technologies to develop solutions that support investigative, audit, research, and operational objectives.

Key Responsibilities:
• Extract, clean, transform, normalize, validate, and analyze structured and unstructured data from multiple enterprise sources.
• Design and develop data science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and predictive analytics solutions, including model development, training, testing, evaluation, refinement, deployment, and maintenance.
• Develop interactive data visualizations, dashboards, reports, and analytical products using tools such as Power BI and related business intelligence platforms.
• Apply advanced analytical techniques including machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), text mining, data mining, statistical modeling, pattern recognition, optimization, and simulation.
• Develop and optimize data solutions using SQL, Python, R, JavaScript, relational databases, data warehouses, data lakes, and data lakehouse environments.
• Build and support ETL/ELT pipelines, data integration processes, data quality frameworks, and analytical datasets.
• Leverage cloud technologies including AWS, Microsoft Azure, Databricks, Data Factory, Data Lake, and Data Lakehouse services.
• Translate business and technical requirements into data models, analytical solutions, technical designs, prototypes, proof-of-concepts, and production-ready implementations.
• Analyze data to identify trends, relationships, anomalies, patterns, and actionable insights that support business, audit, investigative, and operational decisions.
• Work with stakeholders, business owners, database administrators, developers, and IT teams to define requirements, resolve data issues, and deliver analytics solutions.
• Develop comprehensive technical documentation, including requirements, methodologies, data sources, test plans, technical diagrams, user guides, and training materials.
• Troubleshoot, enhance, test, debug, and document existing analytical applications, dashboards, models, and data products.
• Apply data governance, security, quality, access, and continuity-of-operations practices throughout the data analytics lifecycle.
• Present analytical findings, technical briefings, training materials, and project updates to technical teams, leadership, stakeholders, and larger audiences.
• Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing to colleagues on data science methodologies, analytical tools, data quality, data access, and emerging technologies.

Required Skills/Education:
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Analytics, Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related technical discipline.
• 5+ years of professional experience developing data science solutions using programming and scripting languages such as Python, SQL, R, and JavaScript.
• 3+ years of experience applying machine learning, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, robotic process automation, text/data mining, statistical modeling, or advanced mathematical methods.
• 6+ months of experience working with cloud data platforms or services such as AWS, Azure, Databricks, Data Factory, Data Lake, or Data Lakehouse.
• Strong experience with relational databases, SQL querying, data modeling, data warehousing, and data integration.
• Experience developing Power BI dashboards, reports, visualizations, and analytical solutions, including familiarity with DAX and Power Query/M.
• Experience designing and implementing ETL/ELT strategies, data pipelines, data transformations, data validation, and data quality processes.
• Demonstrated ability to transform complex datasets into meaningful business insights and actionable recommendations.
• Experience working with both structured and unstructured data and applying appropriate analytical, statistical, or machine learning techniques.
• Strong understanding of the software development lifecycle, including requirements analysis, design, development, testing, debugging, deployment, and documentation.
• Strong technical writing, documentation, presentation, and stakeholder communication skills.
• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams.

job_description:
Principal Data Scientist - AI for Data and Assessment

Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

Team Description

The AI for Data team builds and ships state of the art machine learning solutions to support data lifecycle within the enterprise. We partner with product, tech and design teams to deliver personalized experiences to our data and platform users to drive productivity and innovation. You will be the driving force to experiment, innovate and create next generation experiences powered by the latest emerging ML technologies.

In this role, you will:
• Partner with a cross-functional team of data scientists, software engineers, and product managers to deliver a product customers love
• Leverage a broad stack of technologies — Python, Conda, AWS, H2O, Spark, and more — to reveal the insights hidden within huge volumes of numeric and textual data
• Build machine learning models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, and implementation
• Flex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals

The Ideal Candidate is:
• Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them.

• Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms.
• Statistically-minded. You’ve built models, validated them, and back tested them. You know how to interpret a confusion matrix or a ROC curve. You have experience with clustering, classification, sentiment analysis, time series, and deep learning.
• A data guru. "Big data" doesn't faze you. You have the skills to retrieve, combine, and analyze data from a variety of sources and structures. You know understanding the data is often the key to great data science.

What are Trust Fund Positions?

Trust Fund positions are unique to the Smithsonian. They are paid for from a variety of sources, including the Smithsonian endowment, revenue from our business activities, donations, grants and contracts. Trust employees are not part of the civil service, nor does trust fund employment lead to Federal status. The salary ranges for trust positions are generally the same as for federal positions and in many cases trust and federal employees work side by side. Trust employees have their own benefit program, which may include Health, Dental & Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Transit/Commuter Benefits, Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance, Annual and Sick Leave, Family Friendly Leave, 403b Retirement Plan, Discounts for Smithsonian Memberships, Museum Stores and Restaurants, Credit Union, Smithsonian Early Enrichment Center (Child Care), Flexible Spending Account (Health & Dependent Care).

Conditions of Employment

• Pass Pre-employment Background Check and Subsequent Background Investigation for position designated.

• Complete a Probationary Period.

• Maintain a Bank Account for Direct Deposit/Electronic Transfer.

• The position is open to all candidates eligible to work in the United States. Proof of eligibility to work in U.S. is not required to apply.

• Applicants must meet all qualification and eligibility requirements within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement.

OVERVIEW
This position is located in Washington, DC, within the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO), Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI), under the Office of the Under Secretary for Science and Research at the Smithsonian Institution (SI).

STRI provides a global platform for research on tropical forests and marine ecosystems, biodiversity, and human well-being.

The ForestGEO program is a global network of scientists and forest research sites dedicated to advancing the long-term study of the world's forests.

The GEO-TREES initiative builds on this network to improve the accuracy and verification of global forest carbon estimates through collaboration among forest research sites worldwide. The Data Scientist supports the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO) and GEO-TREES programs as a liaison between site-based data collection and the development of analytical data products.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Data Management, Scientific Analysis, and Software Programming (50%)

• Performs data-management, computational, and bioinformatics assignments supporting research in tropical biology, ecology, and forestry.

• Develops, implements, modifies, and maintains data-processing pipelines used to process plot-based tree inventory and related ecological data and to derive estimates such as forest woody biomass density.

• Evaluates the performance of existing data-processing pipelines and recommends modifications or improvements based on data characteristics, analytical requirements, user needs, and experience working with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES site teams.

• Develops and modifies computational procedures for analysis of ForestGEO and GEO-TREES scientific data using established data-science principles, methods, and practices.

• Processes, validates, organizes, and manages tree inventory, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS), and Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) data for scientific analysis and long-term storage.

• Supports the archiving and long-term management of scientific datasets to ensure appropriate organization, documentation, accessibility, and usability.

• Develops and maintains data-management solutions and informatics workflows for data acquisition, formatting, validation, processing, analysis, use, and storage.

• Implements established data standards and contributes to the development and modification of data structures and architectures appropriate to assigned projects.

• Writes, tests, documents, troubleshoots, and maintains computer code used in data-processing and analytical workflows.

• Uses programming languages and tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, GIS applications, and related scientific and data-management software.

• Identifies data-quality problems, inconsistencies, missing values, formatting issues, and other anomalies and determines appropriate methods for correcting or documenting them.

• Works with researchers and other technical personnel to ensure that processed data and analyticalproducts meet established scientific and program requirements.

Requirements Gathering and Technical Support (25%)

• Works closely with researchers and program personnel to identify data-processing, analytical, software, and data-management requirements for assigned scientific projects.

• Conducts technical analyses of available methods and alternatives and recommends appropriate software tools, workflows, calculations, and analytical approaches.

• Assists researchers in translating scientific requirements into practical data-processing and

• computational solutions.

• Evaluates existing workflows and recommends modifications when established approaches do not fully address the characteristics of the data or requirements of an assigned project.

• Coordinates with site representatives concerning timelines and technical requirements for acquisition and submission of plot inventory, TLS, ALS, GNSS, and related scientific data.

• Reviews submitted data to determine whether established ForestGEO and GEO-TREES formatting, documentation, and data-quality requirements have been met.

• Works with site personnel to resolve routine and moderately complex data-submission and data-quality problems.

• Coordinates with the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) and other appropriate technical staff to ensure assigned development activities follow applicable systems-development, documentation, version-control, security, and software-development practices.

• Prepares technical documentation describing data-processing workflows, code, data structures, analytical procedures, and related methods.

• Assists in testing new or modified software tools, workflows, and procedures prior to implementation.

Training and Collaboration (25%)

• Develops and provides formal and informal training to researchers, site personnel, and program partners concerning ForestGEO and GEO-TREES data systems, data-management procedures, formatting requirements, data-processing workflows, and related tools.

• Serves as a technical point of contact for tree-inventory teams and other users at assigned ForestGEO and GEO-TREES sites.

• Provides advice, training, troubleshooting assistance, and technical support concerning data collection, formatting, cleaning, validation, processing, documentation, and submission.

• Explains data standards, analytical procedures, software requirements, and data-management practices to researchers and partners with varying levels of technical expertise.

• Collaborates with scientists, data managers, programmers, and other personnel to identify and resolve data-management and processing problems.

• Participates in meetings, working groups, and collaborative activities involving ForestGEO, GEO-TREES, Smithsonian staff, and domestic and international research partners.

• Shares information concerning lessons learned, recurring data problems, workflow improvements, and effective data-management practices with program staff and partners.

Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS
Education and Experience:

• Professional knowledge of and skill in applying a wide range of data-science principles, concepts, methods, and practices sufficient to perform difficult data-management, processing, computational, and analytical assignments involving ecological and forestry data.

• Knowledge of data acquisition, data cleaning, validation, transformation, integration, storage, analysis, visualization, documentation, and reproducible computational workflows.

• Knowledge of computational and data-management methods is required to develop, modify, implement, and maintain processing pipelines for tree inventory, GNSS, ALS, TLS, spatial, and related scientific datasets.

• Knowledge of programming concepts and skill in applying programming languages and analytical tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, and related software to manipulate, process, analyze, and manage scientific data.

• Knowledge of algorithm development, software testing, version control, debugging, documentation, deployment, and maintenance practices is required to support scientific applications and data-processing workflows.

• Knowledge of spatial-data concepts, common spatial-data formats, and GIS software is required to process and evaluate geospatial information associated with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES projects.

• Knowledge of the scientific concepts associated with ecology, tropical biology, forestry, or related environmental sciences sufficient to understand data characteristics, research requirements, analytical objectives, and the relationships among data variables.

• Knowledge to select and modify appropriate data-processing and analytical methods; identify and resolve data-quality problems; evaluate alternative computational approaches; interpret results; develop recommendations; and prepare technical documentation and analytical products.

• Skill adapting or modifying established data-science techniques and procedures to address differences in data structure, quality, collection methods, analytical requirements, or site-specific circumstances.

Job Summary

NORC at the University of Chicago is seeking a qualified Data Scientist I to join the Health Sciences Department to support hospital discharge data processing across states and harmonizing and packaging files into a uniform format. For this role, proficiency in SAS is a requirement. Experience with R or Python is welcome but not essential. Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is preferred, and strong documentation practices are important.

The Data Scientist I supports research, analytics, and data-driven decision-making. This role partners with research teams to collect, manage, analyze, and interpret data to deliver meaningful insights for clients and stakeholders.

The position is responsible for importing, cleaning, standardizing, transforming, and validating data, identifying data quality issues, and developing reports and visualizations. The Data Scientist I may also support data management processes, and proposal development activities. This role works collaboratively in a team-oriented environment.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Location: This is a hybrid role based in either our Chicago Loop or downtown DC office, with a minimum of six days per month in the office. Exceptional remote candidates may be considered as well.

DEPARTMENT: Health Sciences Research

NORC’s Health Sciences staff produce rich data on social priorities including child development and healthy aging, the uses of electronic clinical data in research, and the applications and effectiveness of health information technology.

The Health Sciences team is versatile and experienced in data acquisition, management, technical assistance, and analysis; the use of information technology in health care; and numerous data collection methods. Senior Associate, Data Scientist - Recommendation & Personalization Systems

Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

Team Description:

Join an elite Applied AI team within AI Foundations, operating at the intersection of deep research and massive real-world impact. We are pioneering the next generation of personalized customer experiences across Capital One's web and mobile applications, leveraging our high-scale ML models. Our core mission involves architecting and deploying cutting-edge personalized recommendation engines. This is powered by original research into homegrown Foundation Models, advanced Reinforcement Learning techniques, and a state-of-the-art scalable architecture built for billions of interactions. Our research agenda is at the forefront of the field, actively focusing on areas such as Causal Inference, Transformer-based architectures, and sophisticated Recommender Systems.

• Flex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals

• Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them.

• Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms.

• A data guru. “Big data” doesn’t faze you. You have the skills to retrieve, combine, and analyze data from a variety of sources and structures. You know understanding the data is often the key to great data science.

Why Join GEICO?

At GEICO, we offer a rewarding career where your ambitions are met with endless possibilities.

Every day we honor our iconic brand by offering quality coverage to millions of customers and being there when they need us most. We thrive on relentless innovation to exceed our customers' expectations while making a real impact on local communities nationwide.

Founded in 1936, GEICO is a member of the Berkshire Hathaway family of companies and one of the largest auto insurers in the United States. When you join our company, we want you to feel valued, supported, and proud to work here. That's why we offer the GEICO Pledge: Great Company, Great Culture, Great Rewards, and Great Careers.

GEICO is looking for a Staff Data Scientist, Product Analytics who will provide quantitative rigor, behavioral insight, and a strategic perspective to partners across the organization. As a curious and decision-oriented member of the team, you serve as the analytical thought partner to product, engineering, and design leaders—using data, experimentation, and causal reasoning to help them make better decisions. You will frame the right questions, design the studies that answer them, and translate findings into recommendations that shape what we build. You'll make critical recommendations for Product, Engineering, and senior leadership.

Job Responsibilities:

• Strategic Partnership: Embed with product, engineering, and design leaders as a decision partner—framing ambiguous business questions, pressure-testing roadmap assumptions, and shaping bets before they are committed.

• Metric Frameworks: Define goal metrics, guardrails, and supporting metric trees for your product area. Decompose top-line outcomes into measurable inputs that teams can move.

• Experimentation: Design, power, and analyze A/B and quasi-experiments. Go beyond average treatment effects to understand heterogeneity, long-term impact, novelty effects, and cross-surface interactions.

• Causal Inference: Apply causal methods (difference-in-differences, synthetic control, instrumental variables, propensity scoring, switchback designs) where randomization is not feasible.

• Decision Modeling: Build opportunity sizing, forecasting, and ROI models that scale how the organization makes trade-offs—pricing, growth, retention, and long-range investment decisions.

• Deep Dives: Lead root-cause investigations into user behavior, funnel performance, retention, and engagement. Translate messy signal into clear, defensible recommendations.

• Collaboration: Serve as trusted analytics partner to PMs, designers, and engineers—translate product questions into research designs, analyses, and deliverables.

• Communication: Present findings and recommendations to senior leadership with clarity, structure, and its uncertainty.

• Mentorship & Best Practices: Mentor junior data scientists and analysts. Define internal standards for experiment design, statistical rigor, and reproducible analysis.

Basic Qualifications:

• Experience: 8+ years in product analytics, decision science, data science, or a closely related quantitative role at a technology company, with a track record of influencing product decisions.

• Experimentation: Strong background designing well-powered A/B tests, diagnosing bias and variance issues, handling interference and non-stationarity, and interpreting results under real-world conditions.

• Statistics & Causal Inference: Solid applied statistics foundation with practical experience selecting the right causal method for the question at hand.

• Tools: Advanced SQL and working proficiency in Python or R for analysis, modeling, and reproducible workflows.

• Product Sense: Demonstrated ability to define metric frameworks for a product area, not just operate within frameworks built by others.

• Communication: Clear writing and direct storytelling with data—can produce a one-pager that moves a roadmap and present to executives without losing the nuance.

• Quality Mindset: Disciplined about quantifying what you know, surfacing what you don't, and resisting false precision.

• Education: Bachelor's degree or higher in statistics, economics, computer science, mathematics, operations research, or a related quantitative field—or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Advanced Methods: Bayesian methods, hierarchical models, sequential testing, or uplift modeling experience.

• Domain Experience: Background in growth, pricing, monetization, marketplace, or recommendation problem spaces.

• ML Partnership: Experience working alongside ML engineers on production models, including offline evaluation, online metrics, and guardrails.

• Platform Contributions: Contributions to internal experimentation platforms, metric stores, or measurement tooling.

• Education: MS or PhD in a quantitative discipline.

• Industry: Insurance or financial services experience.
